evidence.claim: An information-commission ruling ordered the NACC to open the asset declarations of Prayut Chan-o-cha and Wissanu Krea-ngam for public inspection, after the NACC refused to disclose the 2019 filings that the two had submitted as evidence.
evidence.title: อ่านฉบับเต็ม คกก.วินิจฉัยการเปิดเผยข้อมูลข่าวสารคณะ3 สั่งป.ป.ช.เปิดเซฟ บิ๊กตู่ -วิษณุ
evidence.excerpt: An information-commission ruling ordered the NACC to open the asset declarations of Prayut Chan-o-cha and Wissanu Krea-ngam for public inspection, after the NACC refused to disclose the 2019 filings that the two had submitted as evidence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The article reproduces the official ruling details and the NACC's refusal rationale with specific case numbers and dates.
evidence.period_fit: The ruling and underlying disclosure dispute were live in the Prayut target-period and still relevant in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Prayut as the office-holder whose own asset filing was being withheld from public inspection; the ruling also concerns Wissanu.
contrary_evidence: NACC argued the evidence filing was private and not legally disclosable.
The article reports the official dispute rather than a finding of substantive corruption.

evidence.claim: Eight months after the formal request, the NACC still had not answered whether the public could inspect Prayut Chan-o-cha's and Wissanu Krea-ngam's 2019 asset accounts.
evidence.title: แค่ส่งคำตอบทางการ “ให้ดูไม่ได้” ยังใช้เวลา 8 เดือนเต็ม ป.ป.ช.ไม่เปิดบัญชีประยุทธ์-วิษณุ
evidence.excerpt: Eight months after the formal request, the NACC still had not answered whether the public could inspect Prayut Chan-o-cha's and Wissanu Krea-ngam's 2019 asset accounts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous coverage of an ongoing official disclosure dispute, though it remains a journalistic summary rather than a primary document.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous with 2022 and squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Prayut because the nondisclosed accounts were his second-term asset filings; the obstruction is institutional rather than a confession of wrongdoing.
contrary_evidence: NACC said the law did not authorize disclosure of filings submitted 'as evidence'.
This shows opacity, not a proven hidden asset or illicit gain.

evidence.claim: After the Constitutional Court suspended Prayuth pending term-limit review, government spokesman Anucha Burapachaisri said Prayuth respected the court's decision, had ceased active duty, and urged the public to respect the decision and avoid further division.
evidence.title: Explainer-How a Thai court suspended Prime Minister Prayuth
evidence.excerpt: After the Constitutional Court suspended Prayuth pending term-limit review, government spokesman Anucha Burapachaisri said Prayuth respected the court's decision, had ceased active duty, and urged the public to respect the decision and avoid further division.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with direct attribution to the government spokesman and the court's official action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's conduct in office because he complied with and publicly acknowledged the court suspension.
contrary_evidence: The suspension itself arose from a contested term-limit petition and opposition efforts to remove him.
Compliance does not answer broader honesty or self-dealing questions.

evidence.claim: The court ruled Prayuth had not exceeded the eight-year limit; in a Facebook post he said his limited time should be used to push important projects, while the opposition said the verdict did not cleanse him and that he had broken his promise not to stay long.
evidence.title: Thai court clears way for PM Prayuth's return from suspension
evidence.excerpt: The court ruled Prayuth had not exceeded the eight-year limit; in a Facebook post he said his limited time should be used to push important projects, while the opposition said the verdict did not cleanse him and that he had broken his promise not to stay long.
evidence.source_locator: period-of-reflection section and the opposition statement near the end of the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a formal court verdict plus contemporaneous quotations from Prayuth and the opposition.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut because it captures his own public framing of continued rule and the opposition's counterclaim about his broken promise.
contrary_evidence: The court ruled in his favor and did not find him disqualified.
The article mixes his statement with opposition criticism, so it is a mixed integrity signal rather than proof of deception.

unresolved_gaps: No Prayut-specific 2022 nuclear or other existential-risk choice is evidenced; the package is mostly inherited treaty and safeguards context.
No direct cabinet-minute or NSC record ties Prayut personally to each 2022 Ukraine or Myanmar diplomatic position.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific police operations, protest policing, and protest-prosecution decisions is limited.
Direct documentary proof of Prayut's personal authorization of spyware or surveillance is absent.
Ruler-level evidence on appointments quality and 2022 rule-setting for competition, property rights, and investment remains thin.
Outcome evidence is stronger than direct ruler attribution across health, education, and social protection.
No direct 2022 evidence of hidden assets, family profit, or proven deception beyond disclosure opacity and allegations.
There is no single consolidated FY2022 execution audit tying the program, implementation, and outcomes back to Prayut's full cabinet-level agenda.
